sources.citation: Naitoro, Katerina. 2019. Morphs in search of meaning: Southeast Solomonic transitive morphology in diachronic perspective. PhD thesis, Australian National University. hdl 1885/163714
sources.note: Malango data come solely from her own fieldnotes (Appendix A, p. 355: 'Malango my fieldnotes'); p. 219: 'The descriptions available for SES languages rarely discuss specifics of stress assignment in verbs with longer suffixes'; p. 350 quotes Ross (p.c.) that SES languages have CV syllables and 'unstressed vowels lose little or no quality'. No statement of Malango stress placement.

sources.citation: Ross, Malcolm D. 1988. Proto Oceanic and the Austronesian languages of Western Melanesia. Pacific Linguistics C-98. Canberra: ANU. (Same work as container 7; additional target coverage: ch. 3 reflex sets pp. 41-92 and Appendix B.6 'South-East Solomonic' p. 410 cite Bauro, Birao, Malango, Dori'o and Kwai from Tryon & Hackman 1983.)
sources.access_detail: a digital copy (available on request); access check: open copy online; also held in print at Harvard (Widener Library (offsite storage), call number PL6201.R67 1988)
sources.harvard_location: Widener Library (offsite storage), call number PL6201 .R67 1988
sources.note: Cited only as a source of lexical reflexes in the Proto-Oceanic consonant chapter (ch. 3) and listed in Appendix B.6 with 'Tryon and Hackman (1983) served as a lexical source for all the languages listed below'; no synchronic phonology or prosody of any South-East Solomonic language is given, and the word 'stress' occurs in the book only on p. 7 (notation) and pp. 86-87 (Ali, North New Guinea cluster).

sources.citation: Tryon, Darrell T. & B. D. Hackman. 1983. Solomon Islands languages: an internal classification. Pacific Linguistics C-72. Canberra: ANU. (Malango = list no. 57)
sources.note: Nothing. Malango appears only as a 324-item wordlist (no. 57, pp. 128-444, no stress marks) and in the phoneme/sound-correspondence tables (sec. 6.1, pp. 82, 90); a full-text search for stress/accent/penult finds only sound-change footnotes ('in unstressed syllables'), no prosodic statement for any Guadalcanal language.
